goal: Create an English educational visual of five selected natural water-cycle processes.
scope: Visual-target case run; final native reconstruction is outside this batch.
copy: Five processes in the natural water cycle
Plants release water vapor through leaves.
Water falls from clouds as rain or snow.
Selected natural processes | Schematic, not to scale
Based on USGS Water Science School

claims.text: Water moves among the atmosphere, surface and subsurface; the cycle has no unique first step.

sourceRefs.locator: Official diagram description and water-cycle processes publication summary

claims.text: Evaporation changes liquid water to vapor; condensation forms liquid droplets; precipitation returns water from clouds.

sourceRefs.locator: Water Science School diagram and processes description

claims.text: Plants release vapor by transpiration; infiltration moves water into soil, with further subsurface movement and return flows.

sourceRefs.locator: Official diagram description: fluxes and groundwater return

claims.text: The new image highlights five natural processes in an illustrative landscape; it is not a complete accounting of human water use or global fluxes.

constraints: Do not depict all water as groundwater or put evaporation arrows downward.
Show only selected natural processes; do not claim there is a mandatory starting step.
No invented percentages, temperatures, rainfall totals, scientific measurements or USGS logo.
A simplified source-based explanation, not a photographic observation; captions carry process meaning.
limits: Human water use and many storage/flux processes are intentionally outside this focused view.
Landscape and arrow scales are explanatory, not measured.
